title: Ukraine Destroys Air Defenses Protecting Putin's Black Sea Palace
excerpt: Ukrainian drone strikes destroyed S-400 and other air defense systems guarding Putin's reported $1.5 billion Gelendzhik compound, with a missile launch pad burning for three hours.
body:
• Ukraine struck and destroyed air defense systems, reportedly including an S-400, protecting Putin's Black Sea palace near Gelendzhik
  • A missile launch pad guarding the compound was reportedly ablaze for three hours after the drone strike
  • Ukraine also struck Buk-M3 systems, military depots, and six UAV control points in the same operation
  • The attack is part of Ukraine's broader campaign to systematically degrade Russian air defenses along the Black Sea coast

Ukraine has destroyed air defense systems protecting Russian President Vladimir Putin's reported palace near Gelendzhik on the Black Sea coast, according to NDTV and Firstpost, with a missile launch pad guarding the compound blazing for three hours after a drone strike.

The strike targeted S-400 air defense systems — Russia's most advanced surface-to-air missile platform — positioned to protect the sprawling compound that has become one of the most controversial symbols of Putin's wealth and power. The palace, estimated to be worth around Rs 13,000 crore (approximately $1.5 billion), sits on the Black Sea coast near the resort city of Gelendzhik in Russia's Krasnodar region.

Scale of the Strike

In the same operation, Ukrainian forces also struck Buk-M3 air defense systems, military depots, and six unmanned aerial vehicle control points, according to reports. The coordinated attack represents a significant escalation in Ukraine's campaign to dismantle Russian air defenses along the Black Sea coast.

https://x.com/Mylovanov/status/2087254596804628935

Footage and reports indicated that the missile launch pad protecting the compound was engulfed in flames for approximately three hours following the drone strike, suggesting a substantial hit on ammunition stores or fuel supplies at the site.

Part of a Broader Campaign

The attack on defenses near Putin's palace is part of Ukraine's systematic effort to degrade Russian air defenses across occupied territories and the Russian coastline. According to the Wall Street Journal, Russian air defenses have become "increasingly impotent" as Ukraine has unleashed an expanded drone campaign.

"This is a classic isolation operation — cutting off all the supply routes for the military, and for the adjacent elements. Air defenses in Crimea have bled out and the navy capabilities that used to be there are gone."

— Alina Frolova, Deputy Chair, Center for Defense Strategies, Kyiv

Ukraine's forces have hit more than 180 vessels and other sea-borne targets around the Crimean peninsula in recent weeks, according to Reuters, while also targeting bridges, railway tracks, fuel depots, ferries, and power installations.

Gelendzhik Under Pressure

The Gelendzhik area has been increasingly targeted by Ukrainian operations. In July 2026, a Ukrainian naval drone sank a Russian patrol ship, the Izumrud, while it was docked near the resort city. Earlier in August, drone debris struck a crowded beach at Arkhipo-Osipovka, a resort village near Putin's compound, killing at least four people including a child and injuring dozens.

The attacks near the palace compound carry symbolic weight beyond their military significance. The sprawling estate was first exposed by Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny in a 2021 investigation that described it as a lavish, fortress-like property complete with a vineyard, amphitheater, and private port. Putin has denied owning the property.

Air Defense Losses Mount

Russia's air defense losses have been significant across the war. Ukraine's defense forces reported hitting twelve S-300/S-400 systems in March 2026 alone, along with ten short- and medium-range systems including Tor, Buk, and Pantsir variants. These losses have created gaps in Russia's ability to control airspace over wide swaths of its territory.

The destruction of air defenses near the Black Sea palace further exposes Russia's southern coast and could embolden Ukraine to expand strikes deeper into Russian territory, analysts say.
